text:
Morgan: heads-up — after yesterday's gpu-plugin roll (k8s-gpu-plugin:v2.4.0) we saw a wave of pods landing on nodes with no usable GPUs in eu-west-2. ~120 jobs affected, lots of NCCL errors and immediate restarts.
Ashish: saw the same pattern in us-west-1 earlier this week after the kernel upgrade. device plugin advertises allocatable before driver probe finishes.
Priya: logs snippet from one node: 
```
I0303 12:01:23.456 kubelet: device-plugin: Registering 8 devices
Dec 03 12:01:23 node kernel: nvidia: module init failed - unresolved symbol
Dec 03 12:01:24 nvidia-driver-manager: probe incomplete, retrying
container: cuda error: no devices found
```
Lin: likely cause = device-plugin daemonset starts and registers quickly on boot, while driver installation (dkms/firmware) is delayed by kernel module build. plugin then reports capacity and scheduler pins pods -> pods crash once container tries to init cuda.
Sasha: current symptoms: pod creates, schedules, then fails with `CUDA_ERROR_NO_DEVICE` or NCCL init failures; node still shows allocatable=gpu:8 which is wrong. Also saw node annotation `gpu-advertised=true` flip-flop.
Priya: repro steps I used: reboot node, watch kubelet + driver-manager. plugin logs: `advertiseDevices()` called before /var/lib/nvidia/probed exists.
Lin: quick mitigation options: 1) make device-plugin delay advertise until driver_ready annotation exists, 2) have driver-manager write node readiness gate, 3) cordon/drain nodes that advertise but fail probe. tradeoffs: delaying advertise reduces usable capacity temporarily (affects throughput/cost).
Morgan: can we do a narrow canary change (daemonset env var) to delay adverstise by a configurable amount? low-risk deploy to single AZ.
Sasha: I tested locally by adding `GPU_PLUGIN_ADVERTISE_DELAY=10` to plugin env; it prevented immediate false-advertise on my VM. Patch idea: add env to ds and default 0.
Ashish: note risk: longer advertise delay -> temporary underutilization and increased queuing for bursty jobs. that has cost + SLO impact. we should measure queue latency at 5/10/20s.
Priya: temporary remediation script to taint nodes without driver_ready so scheduler won't place gpu pods: 
```
kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.annotations.driver_ready!="true") | .metadata.name' | xargs -r -n1 -I{} kubectl taint node {} gpu-missing=true:NoSchedule
```
Lin: better long-term: device-plugin should gate advertise on a node-level marker (e.g., `/var/lib/nvidia/probed` or node annotation `driver.installed=true`). driver-manager can set that once DKMS finishes.
Sasha: I can draft the DS change and test in eu-west-1 canary tomorrow morning. suggestion: advertise delay env + readiness probe from driver-manager that flips node annotation.
DevOpsBot: Incident INC-2026-2103-5 created for tracking (priority: P2). Assigned: eng-infra oncall.
Morgan: plan proposal — (1) roll canary ds with `GPU_PLUGIN_ADVERTISE_DELAY=10` in eu-west-1, (2) run reconciliation script to taint currently mis-advertising nodes, (3) instrument queue latency + GPU cold-start metric, (4) if canary looks good, roll to remaining AZs with 15m gaps.
Ashish: +1. Also add scheduler backoff tuning as fallback to avoid thundering herd when many nodes recover at once.
Priya: I'll run the taint script and collect kernel module build timings from affected nodes, post back with numbers.
Lin: I'll open a PR for plugin gating logic (small change) and include unit tests.
Sasha: ping me when canary is up, I'll run an integration on a synthetic NCCL job set.
Morgan: thanks all — tagging @oncall for awareness. :eyes: we'll reconvene in #eng-infra-status in 2 hours with results.
